content:
Hannah Li: hi all, first-day issue  VPN shows connected via Okta but i can't ssh to the bastion by name (bastion.redwood.internal). ip resolves to 10.10.9.5 which is my home NAS. Any tips?

Diego Morales: welcome! looks like CIDR overlap. what does `ip route` and `cat /etc/resolv.conf` show?

Hannah Li: `ip route` shows default via 192.168.0.1 dev wlan0 and 10.10.0.0/16 via 172.30.4.1 dev tun0. resolv.conf points to 172.30.4.2 but `getent hosts bastion.redwood.internal` returns 10.10.9.5 (my router).

IT Support: yep that's an overlap: your home LAN uses 10.10.0.0/24. Two quick workarounds: 1) use a phone hotspot so your local subnet doesn't collide, or 2) add a host route that forces that host over the tunnel: `sudo ip route add 10.10.9.5/32 via 172.30.4.1 dev tun0` (replace IP with the bastion IP we give you).

Hannah Li: can network-ops tell me the bastion IP?

network-ops: bastion.redwood.internal is 10.10.200.5 in prod. your local 10.10.9.5 is indeed a home device. Run `sudo ip route replace 10.10.200.5/32 via 172.30.4.1 dev tun0` and then `ssh ubuntu@bastion.redwood.internal` should hit the corp host.

Hannah Li: ran the replace command and `ssh ubuntu@bastion.redwood.internal` connects now. thanks!

IT Support: note that host routes won't survive a reconnect in most clients. If you need a persistent fix, use a hotspot or we can issue a NAT egress for your Okta device group. I'll open a ticket if you want that.

infra-bot: Created INFRA-5101: "Onboarded Hannah Li  CIDR overlap; recommend NAT egress for persistent solution".

okta-bot: User Hannah Li (hannah.li@redwood.com) authenticated via Okta at 2026-01-12T11:02:05Z

Hannah Li: temporary fix works for now. i'll add hotspot note to my onboarding checklist and ping IT if this becomes recurring. thanks everyone :wave:
